name: CiteRoute
summary: Generative engine optimisation tool that scores how ready a site is to be cited by AI answer engines, generates agent.json and llms.txt files, and logs AI crawler visits on verified sites; free plan plus paid tracking plans.
best_for: founders and marketers who want to see whether AI crawlers visit their site and how ready their pages look for AI answers, and agencies that want white-label GEO reports for a handful of client sites
skip_if: you want proof of citations rather than a readiness score, you need more than one tracked site without paying agency prices, or you want a vendor with a long track record
honest_knock: The GEO score is CiteRoute's own algorithm, and its terms say outright that it cannot guarantee citations or rankings. The revenue calculator on the home page runs on assumed rates that its footnote calls illustrative. It is a young product with a small public footprint: the home page counts 967+ domains evaluated and 2,043+ scans, and still lists Claude 3.5 among the engines it covers. Real AI-traffic data starts at $79 a month and covers one site. The company operates from Kigali under Rwandan law. Its new citation probe was unreliable in our test on 18 November 2026: it scored 92/100 'Verified Citation' on an answer that said 'I don't have verified information'.

pricing.entry_price_terms: Pro · per month, billed monthly in advance through Lemon Squeezy as merchant of record
pricing.notes: (re-read 2026-11-25 on citeroute.com/pricing with the same four plans, prices, limits and API rates; read 2026-11-18 on citeroute.com/pricing and the home page and in our own test that day; earlier: read 2026-10-13 in a live browser on those pages and the terms of service dated 10 September 2026) Four plans, billed monthly. Free costs nothing and includes 10 GEO scans a month, one monitored buyer prompt in GEO Radar, a two-domain competitor comparison, 3 watchlist domains, the agent.json studio, a basic score report and community support. Pro is $79 a month with a 14-day trial: unlimited scans, 10 monitored prompts, a five-way competitor benchmark, one verified site with the tracking tag and a dashboard of real AI bot and crawler visits, 20 watchlist domains, an API key for 500 requests a day, history charts and priority support. Agency is $249 a month with a 14-day trial: 50 monitored prompts, 10 verified client sites, unlimited watchlist, white-label PDF reports, an embeddable badge and 10,000 API requests a day. Enterprise is custom. API calls beyond the daily plan limit are charged per call: $0.02 for a GEO score, $0.01 for a verification and $0.05 for AI-traffic data. The terms say Lemon Squeezy is the merchant of record and handles VAT and sales tax, subscriptions renew monthly until cancelled, you keep access to the end of the paid month after cancelling, and a full refund can be requested within 14 days of the initial purchase. CiteRoute operates from Kigali, Rwanda, under Rwandan law. Read 18 November 2026, the plans and prices were unchanged; the Free card lists daily automated re-scans as not included, while Pro and Agency include them, and in our test that day the scan page said it rescans every 7 days. The home page now also offers citation probes that check where a domain is cited, with source URLs. In our test the probe was unreliable: it scored 92/100 'Verified Citation' on an answer that said 'I don't have verified information'.

claims.plan: No plan was bought and no trial was started; the pricing page was read without clicking a trial button
claims.comparability: The dossier wording against the probe section of the scan result; the probe was run once on one site.
claims.buying_consequence: The app does show citation labels, but n=1 per engine and a question with the domain name in it is not a measurement of real visibility.

claims.plan: No plan was bought and no trial was started; the pricing page was read without clicking a trial button
claims.comparability: The scan output against the live homepage source on the same day; one page of one site.
claims.buying_consequence: A buyer would add structured data that is already there, and the scores contradict each other.

exit_test.what: We created the account and our AI assistant ran the test in our browser. On 18 November 2026 the session tested the free GEO scan and the citation probe of CiteRoute on a site of our own, in our existing free account. The scan took about 3.5 minutes in 3 steps and gave 81/100 Strong technical readiness, although Google shows the site hardly at all. It reported 0 JSON-LD detected while the homepage has 3 JSON-LD blocks, and some tips are made up (a placeholder wikidata address and an endpoint /api/agent/catalog). The citation probe gave Verified Citation three times on a question that contains the domain name, with n=1 per engine; Claude said it had no verified information and still got 92/100. The prices match the dossier; the dossier says CiteRoute does not measure citations while the app has a probe, and the scan page says rescans every 7 days while Free has daily re-scans struck through. The tracking tag and the AI bot log were not tested, because they need verification by meta tag or DNS. No plan was bought. Account and start: the test used the existing CiteRoute our account, on the Free plan, with the interface in English (no language setting was found). The test started at 09:22 in our own tab. The My sites page showed FREE PLAN and No sites yet. Adding a site needs the CiteRoute Tag and a check of ownership with a meta tag or a DNS TXT record, and the page says that CiteRoute verifies that you control the domain before adding it. That was NOT done, so the tracking tag and the AI bot log were not tested. The dossier name is CiteRoute and the review is on MSS (citeroute-review); the handson folder name and the review slug are the same. The scanned site is a site of our own; its domain is not named in this delivery. Core action: the GEO Scanner (the audit page) works without verification. The domain of our own site was typed in at 09:23, the scan was started, and the result came after about 3.5 minutes (the progress bar stayed at 98% for a long time). It took 3 steps: type the domain, start the scan, start the probe. Result: Technical Readiness Score 81 / 100, labelled Strong technical readiness, with sub scores Tabular and FAQ 77, Content depth 86, Schema 73 and Section hierarchy 88. The scan reported JSON-LD Schemas: 0 detected, 1 H1 and 31 H2, 4,703 words, 0 tables and 0 of 15 points for JSON-LD Schema.org declarations. Check of the scan with curl: the homepage has 3 application/ld+json blocks (Organization, WebSite with a SearchAction and an ItemList with 12 items), so 0 detected is wrong. The 0 tables is right; the llms.txt file exists (HTTP 200) and /.well-known/agent.json gives 404, as the scan says. The Schema sub score of 73/100 stands next to 0 of 15 points for JSON-LD, so the scores contradict each other. Google shows our own site hardly at all, so a label of Strong technical readiness is suspiciously optimistic; readiness is not visibility. The recommendations: add Organization, FAQPage and Dataset JSON-LD and a price table. The Organization example uses sameAs links to our own pages; the second patch example has a placeholder wikidata address ending in Q... and a made-up Crunchbase address; the agent.json example has a made-up endpoint /api/agent/catalog. One tip names the Dataset schema as the fix for HTML data tables and says Embed this JSON-LD on a table tip. These tips must not be copied blindly. The live citation probe (via OpenRouter, preset Brand Authority, no verification needed) asked What are the core capabilities and verified offerings of the domain of our own site; the question itself contains the domain name, so a mention is almost certain. Perplexity Sonar: 92/100, Verified Citation, 100% (n=1), 20 source URLs; the answer mostly fits our site. OpenAI GPT-4o Search: 92/100, Verified Citation, 1 source URL; the answer is a generic invention (pre-built AI applications). Anthropic Claude 3.5: 92/100, Verified Citation, while the answer says I don't have verified information about this site in my training data; it still counts as a citation because it named the URL. Google Gemini: 68/100, Brand Mention Only; the description is wrong (a no-code AI app marketplace). A citation on a question that contains the domain name proves nothing, and n=1 per engine is not a measurement. Deviation from the dossier: the dossier says CiteRoute does not promise or measure specific citations, while the app has a citation probe, with n=1 per engine; no guarantee was seen. Second, the scan page says CiteRoute rescans domains every 7 days automatically, while the Free plan has Daily automated re-scans struck through and Pro has them. Plans, read up to the payment step: Free $0 forever (10 GEO scans per month, GEO Radar 1 monitored buyer prompt, 1-on-1 competitor comparison of 2 domains, 3 watchlist domains, community leaderboard, agent.json Studio, basic score report; struck through: Tracking tag and AI bot traffic detection, API key access, Daily automated re-scans, Weekly email performance digest); Pro $79 a month (unlimited GEO scans, GEO Radar 10 prompts 24/7, 5-way competitor benchmark, 1 verified site with tracking tag, 20 watchlist domains, an AI bot and crawler analytics dashboard, API key with 500 requests a day, history and trend charts, Start 14-day Trial, 14 days free, cancel anytime); Agency $249 a month, Most popular (10 verified client sites, white-label PDF, API 10,000 requests a day, 14 days free); Enterprise Custom. API pricing per call: geo-score $0.02, verify $0.01 and ai-traffic $0.05, and requests beyond the daily plan limits are billed at standard usage rates. The prices and the 14-day trial match the dossier. The Free limit of 10 scans a month was not tested (the counter is not visible on the scan page). No price field is changed here. Checkout: NOT reached. The Pro trial was not started and no payment screen was seen. Cancelling: Free has no subscription. The account menu has API Keys, Third-Party AI Keys and Sign Out, and no button for deleting the account or cancelling a plan; the FAQ says you can upgrade, downgrade or cancel (text cut off). No site was added, so nothing had to be removed. Not tested: the tracking tag and the AI bot log (Pro, 1 verified site; they need verification by meta tag or DNS and a script on the site, which was not allowed), so the dossier group of founders running a single content site is not tested; also API keys, the watchlist, the white-label PDF, share, export, GEO Radar, competitor comparison and Third-Party AI Keys (links external accounts). Clean up: all own tabs were closed; no test site, no script, no DNS or meta change and no external link were made. The scan stays in the Score History of our account; the watchlist was not touched.
exit_test.awkward: The scan said 0 JSON-LD detected on a page that has 3 JSON-LD blocks, and a Schema score of 73/100 stands next to 0 of 15 points for JSON-LD. Some tips contain made-up values (a placeholder wikidata address and an endpoint /api/agent/catalog). The citation probe uses a question that contains your own domain name, so a mention is almost certain, and it uses one try per engine; Claude said it had no verified information and was still labelled Verified Citation. Free has daily re-scans struck through while the scan page says rescans every 7 days.
